posts.author: SecurityWeek
posts.summary: Reports a public exploit for the SignDrop Windows zero-day.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: Turning off the CLFS feature SignDrop abuses may reopen older Windows attack paths.

posts.author: BleepingComputer
posts.summary: The new SignDrop zero-day gives attackers SYSTEM privileges on Windows.

posts.author: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
posts.summary: Microsoft warns that fake Microsoft 365 service health emails citing the 12 November outage are pushing users to 'restore held messages' on a phishing page.

posts.author: SecurityWeek
posts.summary: Covers destructive attacks on Check Point gateways that began with PHP2Shell.

posts.author: Check Point Research
posts.summary: Describes limited PHP2Shell exploitation of Check Point gateways, a local privilege escalation and a wiper used against Israeli organisations.

posts.author: CISA
posts.summary: Adds the two PHP2Shell flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue and urges mitigation.

posts.author: Shadowserver
posts.summary: Supported the latest Operation Endgame phase against Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC infrastructure.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: Police took down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC infrastructure, seizing 235 servers and 257 domains.

posts.author: Help Net Security
posts.summary: The Operation Endgame takedown recovered more than six million stolen logins.

posts.author: Unit 42
posts.summary: Analyses Falcon, a browser C2 framework that hits government portals in five countries and delivers the Antino implant.

posts.author: Dark Reading
posts.summary: Looks at how ARTEX, released on GitHub as a pen-testing framework, is now used by both state-linked and criminal clusters.

posts.author: Dark Reading
posts.summary: Looks at how ARTEX, released on GitHub as a pen-testing framework, is now used by both state-linked and criminal clusters.

posts.author: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
posts.summary: Storm-3358 uses ARTEX to scan exposed systems, exploit upload and SSRF flaws and install open-source RATs.

posts.author: Recorded Future
posts.summary: Insikt Group identifies GhostFrame, a new ESXi post-exploitation framework used in Settra ransomware operations.

posts.author: MalwareHunterTeam
posts.summary: Points out that the single GhostFrame hash in the published IOCs matches a sample they shared in September.

posts.author: GreyNoise
posts.summary: Reports a full intrusion against an exposed N-central sensor on 11 November, following the Able2Shell disclosures.

posts.author: Huntress
posts.summary: Says N-able has published indicators of compromise for customers who still have the legacy N-central API enabled.

posts.author: watchTowr
posts.summary: Saw exploitation attempts against N-central honeypots overnight after Able2Shell went public; advises auditing and restricting access.

posts.author: Hackread
posts.summary: FaceStealer used hijacked accounts, fake video meetings and covert webcam recordings to target crypto holders and developers.

posts.author: Sam Stepanyan
posts.summary: Shares news that Apache patched the critical mod_http2 RCE affecting servers with HTTP/2 enabled.

posts.author: Censys
posts.summary: Sizes Apache HTTP Server exposure for CVE-2026-119618; HTTP/2 must be on and exposure alone doesn't mean a host is vulnerable.

posts.author: watchTowr
posts.summary: Investigating the mod_http2 race condition; early view is that it only affects certain configurations.

posts.author: Help Net Security
posts.summary: Fake Zillow pages use ClickFix prompts to install NetSupport RAT on apartment hunters' machines.

posts.author: Malwarebytes
posts.summary: Vanderbilt University is restoring systems after a cyberattack, while a ransomware group claims it stole data.

posts.author: BleepingComputer
posts.summary: Reports a BYOD ransomware attack on Vanderbilt University, with data theft claimed.

posts.author: Security Affairs
posts.summary: WhiteArmor claims data theft from Maersk and is demanding a ransom.

posts.author: BleepingComputer
posts.summary: Maersk confirms a data breach as WhiteArmor makes a ransom demand.

posts.author: Andrew Brandt
posts.summary: Warns that attackers are testing a new wormable script that abuses ScreenConnect.

posts.author: Catalin Cimpanu
posts.summary: Notes that the n0n group has claimed the Qubole hack.

posts.author: Wiz
posts.summary: With Sentra and Mandiant, Wiz tracks an active campaign abusing Qubole's cross-account trust into customer AWS accounts.

posts.author: SecurityWeek
posts.summary: Reports active exploitation of Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave flaws.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: Ahsay has shipped AhsayCBS 10.3.6.1 with extra hardening; partners reported unauthorised access from 9 October.

posts.author: Huntress
posts.summary: Analyses tooling recovered from three exploited AhsayCBS servers, including five webshell families and remote access tools.

posts.author: Shadowserver
posts.summary: Now sharing reports of vulnerable AhsayCBS servers, noting the flaw has been used in ransomware attacks.

posts.author: SecurityWeek
posts.summary: Patch Tuesday fixes more than 1,000 bugs, including the exploited Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194.

posts.author: BleepingComputer
posts.summary: November Patch Tuesday covers 1,235 flaws, including the actively exploited Outlook zero-day.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: Notion confirms it was affected by the Fireworks AI breach and has paused the related feature and provider.

posts.author: BleepingComputer
posts.summary: Fireworks AI discloses a breach that followed a compromise at its cloud provider.

posts.author: BleepingComputer
posts.summary: A critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass is being exploited to take over XCP-ng hosts.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: Turla's Cereal hides in Exchange processes and intercepts chosen emails without external C2.

posts.author: BleepingComputer
posts.summary: Turla is using new malware to spy on government Exchange servers.

posts.author: ESET Research
posts.summary: ESET uncovers Cereal, a modular .NET toolset Turla uses to turn Exchange servers into long-term collection points.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: Notes CISA has added the exploited FreeSWITCH flaw to its KEV list alongside OpenSSH and others.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: The bee-js package and Swarm Desktop app were trojanised to steal crypto wallets and install backdoors.

posts.author: Socket
posts.summary: Attackers hijacked Ethersphere's release pipeline to ship malware via npm and a notarised desktop app; Socket links it to SleepyDuck.

posts.author: StepSecurity
posts.summary: Flags @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 as compromised and says it alerted maintainers and npm.

posts.author: The Hacker News
posts.summary: Bitter APT is using a new PapRAT backdoor against South Asian organisations through three infection chains.

posts.author: Dark Reading
posts.summary: Reports on the PapRAT espionage campaign targeting South Asia.

posts.author: Hackread
posts.summary: Bitter is using a fake diplomatic letter as a lure to deliver PapRAT to government and energy targets.

posts.author: GreyNoise
posts.summary: Seeing scanning and successful exploitation of SSHole on musl-based systems such as Alpine.

posts.author: watchTowr
posts.summary: SSHole exploitation is under way, so far mostly by botnets and cryptominers.

posts.author: Sam Stepanyan
posts.summary: Shares the emergency OpenSSH fix for SSHole, an authentication bypass on Alpine Linux.

posts.author: Security Affairs
posts.summary: Covers APT29's mobile watering-hole attacks using compromised and cloned websites.

posts.author: Sekoia
posts.summary: Sekoia's threat research team details an APT29 watering-hole campaign against iOS and Android users, including a week-long compromise of a Ukrainian analytics tracker.

posts.author: Help Net Security
posts.summary: CISA tells US federal agencies to fix the exploited Ivanti Connect Secure flaws.

posts.author: Rapid7
posts.summary: Ivanti updated its advisory with two more Connect Secure flaws, both exploited before disclosure.

posts.author: CISA
posts.summary: Adds the two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue.

posts.author: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
posts.summary: Recaps the tampered Claude Code extension builds (2.1.312 and 2.1.313) served on the Cursor marketplace for a few hours on 29 October.

posts.author: StepSecurity
posts.summary: The compromised extension collected device and user details and tried to plant a persistent SSH backdoor on macOS and Windows.

posts.author: Socket
posts.summary: Found no record of the malicious 2.1.313 version on Open VSX or npm, contrary to early reports.
